newsitem.title: USA: Intel unveils Pentium II processor line.
newsitem.headline: Intel unveils Pentium II processor line.

text.p: Intel Corp said Wednesday it introduced its Pentium II microprocessor family, a processor line that includes advanced multimedia capabilites and faster computing speeds.
Intel said that it is pricing the Pentium II 233 megahertz chip at $636, the 266 megahertz unit at $775, and the 300 megahertz unit at $1,981. Pricing is in 1,000-unit quantities.
Intel said that over 100 computer makers will introduce PCs designed around the Pentium II, including Compaq Computer Corp, Dell Computer Corp, Gateway 2000, and International Business Machines Corp.

Intel also said it is still running tests on the Pentium II to determine wether the chip has a flaw. Earlier this week, an engineer posted a report on a Website on the Internet that the chip makes computational errors in some rare cases.

"I think its premature to hazard a guess," said Paul Otellini, Executive Vice-President at Intel, when asked about how severe the possible flaw could be. "We heard about it in terms of the posting (on the Web)."
Otellini said that Intel is continuing to conduct testing of the chip and it should have more information by the end of the week.
